CausalChain: Oxidative stress in liver cells -> Activation of mTOR and kinases -> Phosphorylation of p62 -> Enhanced binding of p62 to Keap1 -> Disruption of Keap1-mediated Nrf2 degradation -> Transient Nrf2 accumulation and nuclear translocation -> Upregulation of protective antioxidant and detoxification genes -> If sustained, chronic p62 accumulation leads to prolonged Nrf2 activation -> Metabolic reprogramming and fibrogenic signaling -> Promotion of liver fibrosis and tumorigenesis
Hypothesis: Selective modulation of p62 phosphorylation can fine-tune the p62-Keap1-Nrf2 axis in hepatocytes, achieving optimal transient Nrf2 activation for cytoprotection while preventing the chronic overactivation that drives metabolic reprogramming and contributes to liver fibrosis and carcinogenesis.
Abstract: Liver diseases are closely tied to the delicate balance of oxidative stress and cellular antioxidant responses, largely orchestrated by the Nrf2 pathway. While transient activation of Nrf2 protects hepatocytes from damage induced by toxins, metabolites, or viral proteins, chronic or uncontrolled activation may inadvertently trigger metabolic reprogramming that promotes fibrosis and tumorigenesis. Recent insights into the role of p62 in modulating Keap1-mediated Nrf2 degradation have highlighted a positive feedback loop that sustains Nrf2 activation. We propose that fine‐tuning the phosphorylation state of p62 can optimize this regulatory axis, permitting necessary cytoprotection without inciting deleterious long‐term effects. This approach may help to reconcile the dualistic nature of Nrf2 in liver pathophysiology and open new avenues for therapeutic intervention in conditions such as non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, alcoholic liver disease, and hepatocellular carcinoma.
